tools.name: deploy_meeting_bot
tools.description: Deploy a transcription bot to a Google Meet, Teams, or Zoom meeting and return the Vexa run ID for that session. Teams needs the full invitation link including the passcode

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: Get the transcript of a meeting, grouped into speaker blocks with timestamps. Refuses rather than return a different session when a vexa_run_id is given and does not match

tools.name: share_transcript
tools.description: Create a public, time limited link for a meeting transcript

tools.name: list_bots
tools.description: List all currently running meeting bots

tools.name: stop_bot
tools.description: Stop and remove a bot from a meeting

notes: BREAKING in 2.0.0: Vexa split its API into two scopes with separate keys. An installation that only has vexa_api_key will fail on every transcript call with HTTP 403 'Insufficient scope for this endpoint'. Add vexa_tx_key to fix it.

get_transcript returns up to 60000 characters, which is more than the 5000 character guideline for templates. A one hour meeting is roughly 70000 characters of speech, and a truncated transcript is useless for writing minutes. Beyond that limit the tool tells the model to fetch the rest with from_time and to_time.
Passages the transcription service cannot attribute are marked '(unknown speaker)' and are never folded into the previous speaker, so the model cannot invent an attribution.

Vexa addresses transcripts by the meeting room ID, and a recurring meeting reuses that ID for every session. GET /transcripts/{platform}/{id} then returns only the MOST RECENT run, silently, even when that run failed with zero segments while an older run holds the real recording. Verified against the live API on 2026-08-13: no query parameter and no alternative endpoint reaches an older run. deploy_meeting_bot therefore returns a run ID and get_transcript refuses when the run it received is not the one asked for. Older sessions of a recurring meeting are not retrievable at all.

The version is bumped automatically. Best practice: call get_page first and pass its Version as expected_version - the update is then refused instead of silently overwriting someone else's edit. Parameters: page_id (required), title (optional), body (optional), expected_version (optional), change_note (optional), content_type (optional). A new body that is much shorter than the current one is refused, because that usually means formatting or other entries were lost; pass allow_shrink=true if it is intended. manifest.name: Open Terminal
manifest.description: Run shell commands, manage files and drive interactive processes on a remote machine via a self-hosted Open Terminal (open-webui/open-terminal) REST API. Works against a local box (via tunnel) or a VPS/Docker sandbox — same skill, only the URL differs.

credentials_required.label: Open Terminal Base URL
credentials_required.hint: Base URL of your Open Terminal instance, e.g. http://172.17.0.1:8000 (VPS Docker) or your public tunnel URL (local machine). No trailing slash needed.

credentials_required.label: Open Terminal API Key
credentials_required.hint: The OPEN_TERMINAL_API_KEY you set when starting Open Terminal (sent as Bearer token).

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Execute a shell command and return stdout/stderr + exit code. Polls until the command finishes. Soft-warns on destructive commands (confirm=true to override).

tools.name: send_input
tools.description: Send text to the stdin of a still-running process (interactive prompts, sudo password, 2FA codes). Use the process_id from a previous run_command.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a text file's contents, optionally a line range.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write text content to a file (creates parent dirs, overwrites if it exists).

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List files and directories at a given path.

tools.name: check_terminal
tools.description: Check that the Open Terminal instance is reachable and report enabled features.
